rows.title: High rents, empty desks: The mystery of downtown Boulder’s office market
rows.standfirst: Downtown Boulder officials fret that 500,000 square feet of office space is officially vacant, and yet much more space is leased, but unused

rows.title: Westcliffe’s conservative newspaper closes as editor calls for a revival: “Watching Fox News doesn’t cut it”
rows.standfirst: The end of the Sangre de Cristo Sentinel shuts the book, for now, on an intense newspaper war that divided Custer County

rows.title: What’s Working: Adams State University and its offspring fuel the San Luis Valley
rows.standfirst: How the school’s $61 million in spending turned into $107 million of economic impact in Southern Colorado. Plus: 500 jobs in Colorado Springs, a new AI nonprofit and more!

rows.title: Hot Colorado labor trend alert: Working past 65
rows.standfirst: 65-plus year olds are part of Colorado’s fastest growing age group of workers. “The 70s are the new 60s,” says one 73-year-old worker from Aurora.

rows.title: Colorado mountain towns see a rare summer slump in visitors as statewide tourism slows
rows.standfirst: Colorado hosted 95.4 million visitors who spent $28.4 billion in 2024, an increase largely from day-trippers. The state is worrying about a decline in international visitors who stay longer, spend more.

rows.title: In Colorado, food stamps will no longer buy soda, sugary drinks
rows.standfirst: The state has plans to expand food assistance benefits to farmers markets, restaurants and for hot grocery food

rows.title: Many new Colorado laws take effect Aug. 6. Here are some you should know about.
rows.standfirst: Labeling meat products. Nuclear energy as a “clean” source. A state mushroom.

rows.title: Keystone property owners sue homeowners association controlled by Vail Resorts
rows.standfirst: Homeowners in the newly formed Town of Keystone argue that the Keystone Neighbourhood Co. unfairly favors Vail Resorts

rows.title: Fiber broadband industry connects in Denver after $42.5B federal program upended
rows.standfirst: Not everyone was glum. Some wireless companies feel like they’re finally getting a chance, while satellite internet remained a big presence in the shadows of Mountain Connect

rows.title: Colorado governor calls special legislative session to deal with nearly $1B budget hole, artificial intelligence law
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers will return to the Capitol on Aug. 21 mainly to deal with the effects of the so-called big, beautiful bill, congressional Republicans’ federal tax and spending measure. They’ll also debate what to do about Colorado’s first-in-the-nation law, which is set to take effect in February.

rows.title: A nuclear reactor at the Denver airport? Here’s what you need to know.
rows.standfirst: Denver’s power needs for massive airport growth mean “no bad ideas,” but is this idea good?

rows.title: A Colorado program that opened the door to large-scale rainwater harvesting likely to end next year
rows.standfirst: Colorado lawmakers created the initiative in 2016, but it generated little interest, with only one Douglas County district stepping up to research and test what could be an important source of renewable water

rows.title: Denver’s minimum wage will be $19.29 in 2026, while Colorado’s wage is expected to top $15
rows.standfirst: Minimum wages in Colorado go up every year based on inflation. Here’s what they’re expected to be next year.

rows.title: EPA cancels $7 billion Solar for All grant program to boost green energy
rows.standfirst: The Biden-era clean energy program included $156 million already awarded in Colorado

rows.title: What’s Working: Google Fiber skips public funding, expands gigabit internet in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Many new neighborhoods getting GFiber internet service already have other options — a good thing, say officials.

rows.title: Scientists chase storms across the Mountain West to study hail’s growing threat
rows.standfirst: The largest study in 40 years has CU and CSU researchers creating a massive database they hope can help them understand the force and features of hail

rows.title: Many Colorado teachers must spend more than 40% of their income on rent
rows.standfirst: A new report takes a closer look at how some districts are stepping into the role of landlord as scarce housing deters many teachers

rows.title: $280 million at stake if Colorado cities don’t start complying with housing policies
rows.standfirst: In a new executive order signed today, Jared Polis declared that beginning Oct. 6, local governments will not be eligible for $280 million in grants across 34 different funding streams unless they are complying with a range of new housing laws

rows.title: Colorado approves up to $14 million to plug oil wells before they end up on state’s “orphan list”
rows.standfirst: The 142 low-producing wells emit “disproportionately high levels of methane emissions,” the state Energy and Carbon Management Commission says

rows.title: Are dogs allowed in Whole Foods stores in Colorado?
rows.standfirst: Except for service animals, dogs and other live animals are prohibited at retail food establishments in Colorado, including grocery stores.

rows.title: Rob Katz’s first move as new CEO at Vail Resorts: benefits for friends of passholders
rows.standfirst: The new Vail Resorts Epic Friend Tickets program gives passholders 6-10 half-priced lift tickets for friends in a “pay it forward type of thing,” says company’s CEO.

rows.title: What’s Working: Why Colorado’s job numbers keep getting revised
rows.standfirst: Revisions may be a bad word now in some circles but local economists explain the importance of updating data.

rows.title: Trump cuts? Not for this tax credit supporting Colorado nonprofits in underserved communities
rows.standfirst: Decades-old New Markets Tax Credit to spur private investment in low-income communities is now permanent. Critics say it benefits the finance industry more than the intended community.

rows.title: Competing visions of how — and how much — to regulate AI as Colorado lawmakers return for their special session
rows.standfirst: The legislature is trying to head off a law that takes effect early next year. They’ll have several different choices of how to do that.

rows.title: Western Slope lawmakers want to pause wolf reintroduction, redirect funding amid Colorado’s $1 billion budget hole
rows.standfirst: The savings would be relatively meager — wolf reintroduction cost Colorado taxpayers $3.5 million last year — but the Democrat leading the measure says it’s about priorities as the legislature contends with a steep drop in state tax revenue

rows.title: 9News parent company Tegna sold to Nexstar, which owns Denver and Colorado Springs Fox affiliates
rows.standfirst: Nexstar CEO says Trump administration initiatives repealing nearly 100 broadcast rules and requirements make the deal worth doing now

rows.title: Colorado River water conservation program remains stalled in US House
rows.standfirst: The program pays volunteers, mostly farmers and ranchers, in four western States to temporarily cut back on their water use in hopes of helping the overstressed water supply in the Colorado River Basin

rows.title: Taxes, AI and health care: Everything you need to know about Colorado’s special legislative session
rows.standfirst: Chief among lawmakers’ tasks is plugging a roughly $750 million hole in the state budget caused by the Republican federal tax and spending bill. But there’s plenty more on the docket.

rows.title: Colorado Democrats condemn sale of 9News’ parent company to owner of Fox31
rows.standfirst: Proponents of the sale argue that former competition rules for TV broadcasting are outdated. Opponents predict layoffs and a threat to independent local news.

rows.title: What’s Working: Why Colorado’s flat home-sale prices may be worse than they look
rows.standfirst: Prices are still relatively high. But behind the scenes, up to 60% of sellers offered concessions and many still trimmed their prices. And then there’s the worsening condo market.

rows.title: Amazon and Starlink awarded 50% of Colorado’s underserved broadband locations
rows.standfirst: The satellite internet services received 8% of awarded funding, while fiber companies won 48% of locations and 91% of funding. Amazon’s low bids meant Colorado is using just over half of its $800 million federal BEAD allocation.

rows.title: Top Senate Democrat shuffles committee to overcome opposition to measure tweaking Colorado’s first-in-the-nation AI law
rows.standfirst: The extraordinary changes to the Senate Appropriations Committee give Democrats a 5-2 advantage on the panel, whereas before they had a 4-3 majority. Democratic state Sen. Jeff Bridges was removed from the committee.

rows.title: Democrats are finalizing deal on tweaks to Colorado’s first-in-the-nation law regulating AI after days of stalled bills
rows.standfirst: If the agreement holds, it would end nearly two years of negotiations on how to try to prevent AI from harming people when they do things like apply for jobs, seek out loans and pursue a college degree

rows.title: Democrats are nixing about $150M in tax breaks to address Colorado’s $750M budget hole. They could be doing more.
rows.standfirst: Every dollar of new revenue Democrats in the legislature find means one less dollar out of the state’s fiscal reserves or that the governor won’t have to cut from existing programs and services

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers abandon special session effort to tweak AI law, will push back start date to June 2026
rows.standfirst: The move came after a deal between consumer advocates, the tech industry and others on how to move forward on the measure fell apart

rows.title: A moon rover is driving around a ranch in southern Colorado. Here’s why.
rows.standfirst: Golden-based Lunar Outpost is competing to be NASA’s human transportation system on the moon later this decade. Its rovers have been kicking up the dust on a rural testing ground in Huerfano County for two years.

rows.title: Democrats end Colorado’s special legislative session by completing punt on AI law into next year
rows.standfirst: Senate Bill 4, which would delay the start date of the AI law to June 30 from February, received final approval Tuesday. It now awaits Gov. Jared Polis’ signature.

rows.title: What the Colorado legislature did during its special session to tackle a $750M budget hole
rows.standfirst: Democrats at the Capitol also pushed back the start date of Colorado’s first-in-the-nation AI law, shored up subsidies on health insurance and tweaked a pair of measures on the November ballot

rows.title: Homeless students, with numbers on the rise, find help in Colorado shelters that resemble college dorms
rows.standfirst: Denver saw a 10% to 25% increase in youth homelessness between 2017-21, according to the journal Pediatrics

rows.title: Xcel Energy is rushing to get wind, solar projects online before door closes on tax credits
rows.standfirst: The utility is about to issue a request for proposals for 4,500 megawatts of generating and battery projects, hoping Colorado regulators OK the projects

rows.title: Why are more Colorado communities trying to protect the night skies?
rows.standfirst: Leadville, Twin Lakes and several state parks hope DarkSky International certification will draw visitors who want to ooh and aah at the stars

rows.title: Colorado, New Mexico, Texas offer fresh settlement proposals in fight over Rio Grande water
rows.standfirst: Settlement hinges on reducing the amount of groundwater pumped along the river in New Mexico to ensure water reaches Texas reliably

rows.title: What’s Working: Rural Colorado taps into flow of geothermal development. Here’s how one family caught the current.
rows.standfirst: It’s more than just a transition from coal and fossil fuels. Plus: Quantum campus opens in Arvada, Colorado unveils new job board, more!
